title: Beneath the Thick but Struggling Clouds
description: Beneath the Thick but Struggling Clouds in Tonic Solfa to ST. AGNES, doh is G: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 4 verses and a piano.
about: These words were printed without an author's name in A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion, compiled by Samuel Longfellow and Samuel Johnson (Boston, 1848), as hymn 295, “Words and Deeds”.
The book printed the words without tunes, marked Common Metre (8.6.8.6), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to ST. AGNES; any other Common Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: Be-neath the thick but strug-gling clouds, We talk of Chris-tian life; The words of Je-sus on our lips, Our hearts with man at strife.

lines: Beneath the thick but struggling clouds,
The words of Jesus on our lips,
Our hearts with man at strife.
Strong souls and willing hands we need,
Remove the gathering dust of years,
We slumber while the present calls,
Wouldst thou see truth? To action wake, —

source: A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion (1848)
licence: Public domain: anonymous words in print by 1848.
credits: Words anonymous, public domain, as printed in A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion (1848); set to ST. AGNES by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
